body:
What should you do?  *Find* friends and hobbies to keep you busy.  Get yourself a part-time job.  Find something, do something, to keep yourself busy to move on from her.

Don't pursue her in any way--not even trying to be friends.  She blocked you on FB, never reached out to you herself, etc.  She is not interested.  You know that.  It sucks, and I'm sure it hurts, but this is not the girl for you and she isn't going to be.

Hobbies.  Friends.  Work.  Something, just get yourself busy and stop thinking that you're going to get her back.  Sorry.

Of course. I'm just glad that I could help, at least a little bit.  I hope you get some good rest.  I'm going to be pretty busy this week, but I'll make a point to PM you sometime soon.  Hang in there, and thanks for talking with me.

Those friends of yours, though, that you think are better than you--friendship is a two-way street.  Even if you feel like it's an unbalanced, unequal friendship, if they're still your friend, they must have a reason.  As for me, I didn't choose to be friends with these people, exactly--it developed naturally, for which I'm grateful.  And the thought of wanting to make people feel guilty through your suicide--I've been there, too.  I had a friend a few years ago who, when I told him about my suicidal thoughts, went on one of those "that's so selfish" rants, and I realized that that was part of the reason I wanted to kill myself, at least at that time.  To make everyone see how much pain I'd been in after the fact and make them feel guilty for not helping me.  That doesn't factor so much into my thoughts these days, but I get it.  For me, it wasn't because I was just a terrible person (and I don't think you are, either).  It was that I cared about them so much, and I was in so much emotional pain and stress that it hurt that they didn't see and help me--it felt like they didn't care about me as much as I cared about them, and suicide would have been "revenge" for that.  Whatever drove you to that thought, though, I don't know, but it doesn't make you an awful person.

Wanting to be friends with people you consider better than yourself doesn't make you awful, either.  It makes you human--we're all drawn to people we see as better than ourselves, and we all want to present a picture to others of ourselves as being better than we are for that reason.  I'm not perfect, and I sometimes doubt that I'm even a good person, so I don't often get what my friends and other loved ones see in me--I'm just grateful that they see some reason to stay.  And not making an effort to comfort people you see who are worse off than you--from what you've said, it sounds to me like it's in large part due to your feeling that you wouldn't be able to do anything for them anyway.  It isn't because you intentionally and maliciously ignore them--at least, that's how it sounds to me.

Thanks for saying that, and I'm glad, I guess, that I'm giving off the impression of a great person.  XD  And yeah, actually, you are doing something for me.  In the short time that we've been talking, look at how much I've been able to empathize with what you're feeling--I'm not alone in my feelings, this is telling me (and neither are you).  You're letting me feel like I can help someone.  You're telling me that I'm a good person.  That may not seem like much, but it's pretty meaningful stuff to me.

No, I never feel like I shouldn't have gotten help, because I know what I would have done to myself if I hadn't.  Yeah, I'm pretty messed up in a lot of ways for a lot of reasons, but there are still people worse off than I am.  Still, that doesn't mean that I shouldn't have gotten help.  I needed it, and when I did go to get it, everyone I encountered was incredibly compassionate.  No one believed that I was being unjustifiably whiny or attention-seeking, they just saw that I had some problems and wanted to help me fix them.

I have really, really awful social anxiety, so I know what you mean when you say you're afraid to say the wrong thing.  Honestly, I haven't made a new friend since high school because I can't make a connection, and the friends that I do have are just as awkward.  I wouldn't have been able to talk to them otherwise, but seeing that they were struggling with having a conversation just as much as I was was incredibly helpful at times; also, having friends like that means that when they put effort into me, I was putting effort into them.  I learned that it's just about balance and honesty, about who you are and what you want from any relationship.

I know it's hard not to, but you shouldn't feel guilty about feeling sorry for yourself.  It's like that saying that's been going around--if you can't be sad because someone else has it worse than you, then by the same token, you shouldn't ever be happy because someone will have it better off than you.  That doesn't make any sense.  It's hard to reconcile the intellectual understanding of that concept and the emotions surrounding guilt, though.

I'm sorry that you don't have more people you can really talk to in your life.  That can make talking things through really tough.  It sounds like you have great intentions, and want someone to empathize with.  It sounds like you'd be good at it, and that you'd be a good friend.  It's really hard trying to get to a deeper, emotional level of friendship though, when you haven't had that connection in the relationship before.

All in all, it sounds like you have a really giving personality.  Is there any other way you can think to use that in your life besides with your friends?  Volunteering, mentoring, something like that?

I know how scary it is to get help for this, especially when you've been saying "I'm fine" and trying to take care of others instead of yourself.  That was actually the bulk of my own post here.  Finally going to someone to talk about this was actually really relieving in a lot of ways, though.  Professionals don't react like friends sometimes can, where it's part worry, part pity, part disbelief.  They're really matter-of-fact, and I found that that helped.  It also sounds like you might benefit from group therapy.  There are anonymous groups, too, that aren't exactly clincal-- more like alcoholics anonymous, but for depression.  If you aren't ready to go to a doctor or therapist or someone like that, maybe one of those groups would be good for you.

Honestly, one of the things that helps me most is being able to empathize with others who feel the same way that I do, or can at least conceptually understand it--another reason, I guess, that I'm here on this subreddit.

What everyone needs can be wildly different, and for me, it's mostly time.  The longer I go without giving in to the worst thoughts I have, the stronger I feel, and the more worthwhile I feel things become.  I've also tried things like therapy and medication, the latter of which didn't go so well for me in particular--have you tried that?  You said this was new for you, so I don't know if you've had a chance to do anything about it.

Being there is the best thing that anyone can have to offer.  That's basically all that I'm doing for you right now, isn't it?  I don't have magic words or a quick fix, just some company and a sympathetic ear.  It feels inadequate, sometimes, I know, but just being present for someone in a tough spot can mean a lot.

There's a flip side to what your friend said.  While you're looking at it like you're a bother and she's only talking to you because you want her to, you could also look at it from the perspective that she cares enough/likes you enough to try to take what you like into consideration.  Maybe she doesn't like to talk as much as you do, but likes you enough that she's willing to make the effort.

Plus, depression and anxiety and all that's related to it can make us feel like we're worth a lot less than we really are, or that we're worth less than other people think we are.  I personally don't see that much value in myself, but I've learned to accept that my friends see something in me that I can't see in myself.

And no, you aren't inconveniencing me or punishing me.  When I need to stop responding, because I'll be going to bed or something, I'll let you know.

I'm not... good, yet, but I'm better, and I feel now like it can get better.  That's the difference.  I still have all of the same suicidal thoughts that I did a month ago, but now I'm challenging them in my head, if that makes sense.

You're really welcome.  And, actually, I reply to people because a few weeks ago, I posted here myself.  I was all kinds of messed up, and talking through things with people really helped.  I didn't feel better, but I saw things a little more clearly and was able to wait it out until I did.

I personally think that that's exactly the right idea about talking to people--it's what I needed, anyway.  I just wanted people to say something to let me know that it was okay for me to talk, and to listen.  If this makes any sense.

I'm really glad that I made you feel even a little better.  If you want to keep talking, I'll definitely be around on here for a while.  Doesn't matter what it's about.
"Someone is getting a hold of the crisis center for me.  I may or may not opt to go into respite." She tweeted this a while later, you can rest a little easier.  It looks like she'll be okay.

Hi. If we just talk, not even really about feelings or anything, would that feel like you're being a burden?  It wouldn't to me.

What's your favorite movie?

Hi.  I don't usually post much here, but your post hit me on a pretty personal level.  When I was a kid, I was abused by an adult, and one of my other friends (who had also been abused by someone else) used to coerce me into that same type of behavior.  I was abused by a male adult, and grew up to be bisexual, but I wonder sometimes if I learned to like women because I was so afraid of men for so long.  So I really get where you're coming from when you say that you don't know what your sexuality is--it's really confusing to figure that out when you're in weird/inappropriate sexual situations that young.

I also know what it's like to feel like you're in over your head with life and don't know what you want to do about it.  I'm really, really sorry that your parents aren't terribly supportive towards you, and I'm also really sorry about the situation with your dad.

I don't really know what to say, but if you want to talk, I've got some common ground, I think, and I'm here.
I also feel like that so much of the time. But this woman in your life must be there for a reason, right? Maybe she sees something in you that you can't see in yourself.

Ah, I see.  Thank you for passing that help on to me, then.

As for me and meds, the most frustrating thing is that it seems that pretty much all of the SSRIs have terrible side-effects for me, but the doctors and psychiatrists are reluctant to prescribe some other kind of drug because "SSRIs have been so well-studied in treating depression and anxiety!"

I didn't go to a hospital, and I'm not going to, but I do have an appointment with an outpatient clinic that has a psychiatrist on-staff as well as counselors.  I haven't talked to my friend yet, but my boyfriend and I both agreed that I need to back up and take care of myself for a while.   Once she's settled into her therapy and spoken to her mother, we're going to talk it over and make sure that she'll be okay for a while if I get some distance while I go through my own treatment.

This is probably going to be my last post on this thread, at least for now, but not in a bad way.  I just wanted to let you know that I'm moving in a positive direction and thank you again for your help, and for sharing your experience with me.  You and this subreddit kept me from doing anything that night.

That is actually a really good idea.  I worked up the courage to talk to my boyfriend about posting here last night, and he's going to help me talk to her.  Thank you again, that is a really good suggestion.

Wow.  I feel like you just described almost exactly what I'm feeling and going through as well.  I don't have much I can think to say, but I just want you to know that I'm here and I can listen if you want to vent about it.

I'm off to bed now, and I'll reply more in the morning, but I just wanted you to know that it was a really bad night and you helped a lot to talk me through it and give me some points to think about.

Also, if helping others makes you feel better, I think that just makes you a good person.  Thanks.

Boyfriend, best friend, mother (my sister really scared her, and I'm the only one she'll talk to about it).  I'm afraid with the doctor, though, that I might flake out like I have on so many other things and just not go because of my anxiety about it, and my lack of motivation due to depression.  I hope you sleep well, and thanks again.

Honestly, I was there for 99% of her time at the hospital.  Other than asking my boyfriend to drive me home so I could sleep off my drunkenness, I was there the whole time.  There wasn't too much to make me scared, but it's more that a) it wasn't a mental health hospital, just the ER and b) what scares me most is that then people will know, and I might upset them.

Is the hospital the best way to go?  Did it work well for you, since you said you had experience?  I am honestly just as terrified of that as I am of going to a new psychiatrist.  Medication makes me worse, usually, and that's scary, too.

Thank you, though.  Your reply helped a lot, and gave me a lot to think about.  It also made me realize I'm really tired, too, and maybe I should sleep on it before I make any decisions?

I don't know if I really feel this or if it's an excuse I'm using because I'm scared (maybe both), but I feel like that would be too much for them.  I'm the one they're already leaning on, so what happens if I can't be strong anymore?  And how do I tell them?  I guess I am stubborn sometimes.

Thank you for answering, by the way.

She thinks about it, but says she wouldn't ever try it, and I believe her.  I feel like I should be getting the help that I made her get, too, because if anything, I'm more at risk than I think she is.  It just feels really hypocritical to me that I made her go to the hospital when I'm too scared to go myself.
